utility.notes: The City of Healdsburg's own Electric Department is the city's municipal electric utility, handling power procurement, regulatory compliance, and conservation programs. Sonoma Clean Power's own service description explicitly excludes Healdsburg from its territory, consistent with Healdsburg having its own municipal utility.

value.name: City of Healdsburg Electric Department
value.notes: The Electric Department is a vertically-integrated municipal utility (like Palo Alto's CPAU, Silicon Valley Power, Riverside Public Utilities, and Glendale Water and Power) — it procures and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA. Sonoma Clean Power (the CCA serving most of Sonoma County) explicitly excludes Healdsburg from its service area.

interconnection_url.notes: The City of Healdsburg's own Electric Department page; interconnection is handled directly by the municipal utility rather than a separate IOU.

battery_programs.notes: Confirmed absence, not an unresearched gap: the City's own Electric Department FAQ directly states 'No, the City does not have solar or battery installation rebates,' and points customers to www.SmartLivingHealdsburg.org for other energy programs/incentives (not independently verified this session).

value.name: Three uniform-sized paper plan sets (for in-person submittals)

value: Once the solar installation is complete, schedule the required final on-site inspection by calling the City of Healdsburg at 707-431-3346 during working hours
Inspection requests received are typically scheduled for the next business day
The approved plans and permit must be onsite and available to show conformance with all requirements at the time of inspection
inspection_steps.notes: Per the City's own 'Expedited Residential Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems: Plan Review, Fees, and Inspections' handout, Section 5 (Inspections).

value.notes: Permits are approved in a timely manner, usually 1 to 3 days, once documentation is correctly and fully submitted. The City's own PV handout further specifies: applications complying with submittal requirements may be approved 'over the counter' at the Building office, and 'Permits not approved over the counter should be reviewed within 1 to 3 days.'
